//: TypeScript 6.0 baseline. Its defaults are already the modern ones - strict, module
esnext, target es2025 - so this file only states what differs or what 6.0 stopped
inferring for us. Two of those are easy to miss and produce confusing failures:
- `types` now defaults to [] rather than auto-discovering @types/*, so ambient Node
globals are invisible unless a package names them.
- `baseUrl` is deprecated and `moduleResolution: node` is gone. Path mappings carry
their own prefixes and resolution is nodenext or bundler per package.
Do not reintroduce either. See AGENTS.md 5.1 for the pinned-version rationale.
There is no bundler and no build step for the server: Node 24+ runs .ts directly
by stripping types. That imposes three settings together, and removing any one of
- imports must carry an explicit .ts extension (Node resolves the real file),
- allowImportingTsExtensions permits that, which requires noEmit,
- verbatimModuleSyntax forces `import type` to be marked, because a stripper
cannot know which imports were types and would leave a runtime import of a
module that only ever existed at the type level.
